strokes.text: Manages one filter of any installed kind on a source, scene or group, with the settings you choose to manage.
OBS has no filter UUID, so a filter is identified by its parent UUID together with its name.
Only one resource may own a given parent and filter name; do not declare this resource over a filter that a typed filter resource manages.
The `settings_json` object owns exactly its top-level keys, with the same rules as @resources/source.
OBS creates every filter enabled and the provider then sets the declared state, so a plugin may briefly see a filter enabled that is declared with `enabled` false.
Import with a JSON object that names the collection, parent UUID, parent name, filter name, kind and the settings to manage:

glazes.kind: OBS filter kind, for example `color_filter_v2`. It must be a kind the running OBS has registered. Changing it replaces the resource.
glazes.name: Name of the filter as shown in OBS. Changing it replaces the resource.
glazes.settings_json: JSON object of managed top-level settings. Writes overlay these keys; omitted keys retain OBS values. Nested objects are managed as whole values.
